title: SecOps-NG DPIA Evidence Artifact
description: Typed shape for one evidence artifact emitted by the data_protection_impact_assessment (DPIA) evidence stream. One artifact is produced per (workflow_id, execution_id) cycle of the F-WF-DPIA data_protection_impact_assessment workflow — the ex-ante GDPR Article 35 assessment lane, distinct from the after-the-fact breach-notification lane (Art. 33-34) and the subject-initiated rights lane (Art. 15-22). Carries the Article 35(3) screening outcome, the residual-risk verdict feeding the Article 36(1) prior-consultation gate, the Data Protection Officer consultation record (Art. 35(2)), and the boolean article_36_prior_consultation_flag toggled when residual risk crosses the operator's threshold. Public-bar artifact: operator-side strings (owner labels, submission references, DPO handle) MUST stay role-shaped or URN-shaped; individual personal names are out of scope per AGENTS.md §3. Byte-parity: the compile target (n8n / Temporal / LangGraph) is deliberately absent from the artifact_id derivation so a replay under a different target produces the identical artifact_id for the same (workflow_id, execution_id, captured_at) input.

schema_version.description: Pinned schema version. Lets a consumer reject artifacts produced under an older schema once breaking changes ship.

artifact_id.description: Stable per-artifact identifier. Convention: SHA-256 hex digest of `<workflow_id>|<execution_id>|<captured_at>` (UTF-8, single pipe separators, no surrounding whitespace). MUST NOT key on compile_target — the artifact_id is the byte-parity anchor across the n8n / Temporal / LangGraph reference emitters, so a replay of the same (workflow_id, execution_id, captured_at) triple under any target produces identical bytes. Deterministic on those three inputs; dedup is trivial.

stream.description: Identifies which evidence stream produced the artifact. Constant on this schema.

workflow_id.description: Stable workflow identifier. Fixed value `data_protection_impact_assessment` for artifacts produced by the F-WF-DPIA playbook; kept as a field (rather than a schema const) so downstream aggregators can partition evidence by workflow without a schema branch.

execution_id.description: Per-execution identifier issued by the compile target's workflow runtime (n8n execution id, Temporal workflow run id, LangGraph thread/checkpoint id). Re-runs of the same DPIA case produce distinct execution_ids — the operator's Article 5(2) accountability chain treats re-emission as evidentiary signal rather than dedup waste.

regulation_refs.description: Pins to the upstream regulatory mapping entries this artifact helps satisfy (e.g. gdpr:art-35, gdpr:art-35-3, gdpr:art-35-7, gdpr:art-36-1, gdpr:art-5-2-accountability). At least one entry — an artifact with no regulatory anchor is not DPIA evidence in the F-WF-DPIA sense. Joins back into content/mappings/<regime>/*.yaml via the `id` field.

control_refs.description: Control stable-ids attested by this artifact. Same shape every other layer of the content model uses. At least one — typically `control.dpia_lifecycle@v1` and/or `control.dpia_prior_consultation@v1`.

screening_outcome.description: Deterministic output of the F-WF-DPIA `screen_dpia_triggers` step against Article 35(3) mandatory-DPIA triggers and the operator's supervisory-authority Article 35(4) blacklist. `dpia_required` records whether the screening concluded a full DPIA is mandatory; `triggers_matched` is the ordered list of trigger stable-ids that fired (e.g. `art-35-3-a-systematic-monitoring`, `art-35-3-b-special-categories`, `art-35-3-c-public-monitoring`, `art-35-4-blacklist:<row-id>`); `screened_at` records when the screening step ran.

dpia_required.description: Screening verdict. When false the workflow takes the audit-close branch and no downstream Article 35(7) assessment is produced; when true the full lifecycle continues.

triggers_matched.description: Ordered list of trigger stable-ids that fired against the input processing description. Empty list is legal when dpia_required is false and the operator's threshold policy still requires evidence emission (e.g. a documented near-miss).

screened_at.description: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp at which the screening step ran.

notes.description: Optional plain-language reviewer note. Public-bar text: no operator branding, no individual names.

residual_risk_verdict.description: Deterministic output of the F-WF-DPIA `identify_and_document_mitigations` → residual-risk step. `band` is a coarse three-value bucket the Article 36(1) prior-consultation gate keys on; `rationale` is a short plain-language line the reviewer reads; `evaluated_at` records when the verdict was reached.

band.description: Coarse residual-risk band after mitigations. `low` and `medium` do NOT trigger Article 36(1) prior consultation; `high` does. The operator's threshold policy MAY promote `medium` to `high` — the promoted verdict is what lands here.

rationale.description: One-paragraph plain-language rationale for the band. Public-bar text: no operator branding, no individual names.

evaluated_at.description: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp at which the residual-risk verdict was reached.

dpo_consultation_record.description: Record of the Data Protection Officer consultation required by GDPR Article 35(2). Role-shaped: the DPO is referenced by a working-group mailbox or role handle, never by an individual personal name. `consulted` is the boolean signal; `dpo_role` and `consulted_at` are required when consulted is true; `advice_summary` is a short plain-language summary the reviewer reads.

consulted.description: Whether a DPO consultation was performed for this DPIA cycle. False is legal in the audit-close branch (dpia_required=false); Article 35(2) makes consultation mandatory when a DPO is designated and a DPIA is required.

dpo_role.description: Role-shaped identifier for the consulted DPO (e.g. 'dpo@example.org', 'data-protection-office'). Personal names are not used.

consulted_at.description: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp at which the DPO consultation was recorded.

advice_summary.description: One-paragraph plain-language summary of the DPO's advice. Public-bar text: no operator branding, no individual names.

consultation_reference.description: Optional operator-side reference (URN, ticket id, document handle) pointing to the durable consultation record.

article_36_prior_consultation_flag.description: Boolean flag toggled when the residual-risk verdict crosses the operator's threshold for Article 36(1) prior consultation with the supervisory authority. Downstream consumers (the pre-consultation submission chain, the KRI on consultation lead-time) key on this single boolean; the underlying rationale lives in residual_risk_verdict.

captured_at.description: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp at which this DPIA cycle's evidence artifact was captured. Stable input to artifact_id — alongside workflow_id and execution_id, this is one of the three fields that byte-parity keys on.

provenance.description: Where this artifact came from. Mirrors the provenance pattern used by content/controls/*.yaml so a reviewer can re-derive the chain back to source. Optional: audit-close artifacts MAY omit provenance when no runtime handle exists.

source_url.description: URL of the workflow run (or workflow-content source) that produced this artifact. Compile targets may use their own run-id URLs; the URL itself is opaque to this schema.

captured_at.description: ISO-8601 date or date-time matching the artifact-level captured_at.

commit_sha.description: Optional commit SHA of the content snapshot the workflow walked.

owner.description: Optional dated ownership pointer. Role-shaped — a working-group mailbox, a generic role title, or a community handle. Individual personal names are out of scope per AGENTS.md §3 and rejected here as a matter of schema discipline.

retention.description: Optional ISO-8601 duration recording the retention the operator commits this artifact to (e.g. P3Y).
